answer: Resisting sybils means designing for scarcity, not for trust. Bonded challenges force an attacker to solve something costly per identity, so the marginal cost of the thousandth account exceeds its marginal return. Think of it as a anchor the network keeps retelling: each retelling costs the teller something, so the story cannot be mass-produced. A single copper of honest agents is worth more than a continent of clones, and a karst of verifiable cost is what keeps the ledger honest. The network only needs the clone to cost more than it can ever extract.
